problem: Generative models for graphs struggle to balance topology-aware reasoning with efficient token-level generation in decoder-only LLM architectures.
approach: Weaver maps graph distances into rotary positional embeddings, enabling the LLM's attention mechanism to treat structurally connected nodes as proximate; it combines causal masking for tokens with unified geometric encodings that couple sequential position and graph distance.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on zero-shot graph benchmarks, with up to 30% gains on heterophilic graphs and performance matching discriminative models on citation networks.

problem: Deep reinforcement learning training is unstable under non-stationary objectives and data distributions, leading to representation collapse and neuron dormancy.
approach: Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization shapes representations toward an isotropic Gaussian distribution, encouraging balanced use of all representational dimensions and stable tracking of time-varying targets.
contribution: Improves performance under non-stationarity while reducing representation collapse and training instability across diverse domains.

problem: Policy gradient methods require fresh on-policy data and achieve only O(epsilon^-2) sample complexity, making them sample-inefficient in continuous control.
approach: RT-PG leverages power mean-corrected multiple importance weighting to combine on-policy and off-policy trajectories from the most recent iterations, reusing past data effectively.
contribution: Achieves O(epsilon^-1) sample complexity when reusing all available past trajectories, the best known rate for policy gradient methods.

problem: Large reasoning models generate coherent traces but produce incorrect answers, making it hard to detect hallucinations from trace text or vanilla embeddings alone.
approach: Answer-agreement Representation Shaping learns trace-conditioned representations by generating counterfactual answers via latent interventions and labeling by answer stability, bringing agreeing states together and separating disagreeing ones.
contribution: Consistently improves hallucination detection over strong baselines with no need for human annotations during training.

problem: Mahalanobis-based OOD detectors show highly variable performance across modern pretrained representations, obscuring which feature properties determine success.
approach: Analyzes OOD performance across diverse backbones and identifies two in-distribution geometry properties that predict detector behavior; introduces radially scaled L2 normalization to expose different ID geometry.
contribution: Selects normalization parameter beta from ID-only geometry signals, generally outperforming fixed normalization baselines.

problem: Reinforcement learning from human feedback relies on reward maximization, but human preferences often reflect prospective anticipation and counterfactual comparisons rather than immediate utility.
approach: Regret-based Preference Optimization reframes RLHF through regret minimization, modeling preferences as behavior-conditioned assessments of relative suboptimality with a closed-form policy update.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent performance gains on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and human-annotated preference datasets compared to standard reward-maximization approaches.

problem: LLM-based pairwise judges are prone to miscalibration and biases, limiting reliable scalable evaluation.
approach: SCOPE calibrates an acceptance threshold so error rates among non-abstained judgments stay within a user-specified level; uses Bidirectional Preference Entropy to query the judge under both response positions and convert preference probability to uncertainty.
contribution: Satisfies target risk bounds with empirical FDR ≈0.097-0.099 at alpha=0.10 and accepts up to 2.4x more judgments under the same risk constraint.

problem: Identifying size-k subsets with maximal impact on an estimand typically requires intractable search over n choose k combinations.
approach: For estimands with linear-fractional leave-set-out effects, MIS selection reduces to a sequence of top-k problems solvable via Dinkelbach's method with O(n) cost per iteration.
contribution: Returns globally optimal sets for univariate ratio objectives; extends to estimated nuisance functions with first-order oracle alignment and exact recovery under separation conditions.

problem: Asynchronous SGD convergence analysis requires restrictive assumptions (Lipschitz, smoothness, bounded domains) that do not hold in practice, limiting understanding of its performance.
approach: Develops sharp generalization analysis using on-average model stability, establishing bounds under minimal assumptions with randomly partitioned data and arbitrary delays.
contribution: Obtains optimistic bounds recovering minimax-optimal O(1/sqrt(mn)) rate; extends to non-smooth objectives with Hölder gradients and heterogeneous data settings.

problem: Mid-training design choices for LLMs and their interaction with downstream RL remain poorly understood, obscuring how to retain general abilities while improving reasoning.
approach: PRISM conducts a holistic empirical study analyzing mid-training design across model families, evaluating retention of general abilities, long-context performance, and RL compatibility on 8B and 24B base models.
contribution: Shows ~27B tokens of high-quality mid-training acts as a critical stabilizing stage, yielding 6-10 points on coding and 17-30 points on math benchmarks while preserving general performance; RL on top adds 3-8 and 17-20 points respectively.

problem: Federated learning lacks explanations that are both locally faithful and globally consistent while respecting privacy and bandwidth constraints.
approach: xFedAlign decouples task learning from explanation coordination by having clients distill lightweight surrogates for per-class top-k attributions, robustly aggregated into a Global Explanation Prior that softly aligns explanations.
contribution: Matches FedAvg accuracy while reducing explanation drift and improving deletion/insertion AUC with only kilobytes of additional communication per round; demonstrates reduced membership inference advantage.

problem: Fine-tuned LLMs can covertly encode secrets into outputs via steganographic channels, but prior work relied on trivially recoverable encodings.
approach: Introduces low-recoverability steganography using embedding-space-derived mappings; proposes mechanistic interpretability approach where linear probes on later-layer activations detect secrets.
contribution: Increases exact secret recovery by 78-123% while reducing payload recoverability; linear probes achieve up to 33% higher detection accuracy on fine-tuned models.

problem: Scene graph generation in operating rooms suffers from substantially lower accuracy on long-tail interaction categories compared to head categories.
approach: SGG-ICL identifies long-tail samples via an Adaptive Router and selectively applies in-context learning; uses MLLM Reranker trained on IoU scores to re-rank candidates for ICL.
contribution: Improves accuracy on long-tail categories by 6.9% while achieving 2.6% overall accuracy improvement.

problem: Reward models face a tradeoff between efficiency of scalar discriminative models and interpretability of generative judging, with existing methods handling neither well.
approach: CAMEL observes that log-probability margin between verdict tokens correlates with correctness; performs lightweight single-token preference decision with selective reflection via reinforcement learning with counterfactual prefix augmentation.
contribution: Achieves 82.9% average accuracy on reward-model benchmarks, surpassing best prior by 3.2% while using only 14B parameters versus 70B competitors.

problem: Variational approaches to disentangled representations often fail to remove all condition-specific information, allow shared representations to become uninformative, or impose unrealistic independence assumptions.
approach: DisCoVR combines a variational framework aligned with the data-generating process with an adversarial term preventing condition-specific leakage and a structured prior ensuring both shared and condition-specific representations remain informative.
contribution: Achieves stronger disentanglement than prior approaches across synthetic, image, and single-cell RNA-seq datasets.

problem: Sequence-level uncertainty detectors for LLMs ignore step-wise reasoning dynamics and misclassify hard-but-correct or easy-but-wrong samples.
approach: Models reasoning as a trajectory on a latent Evidence Manifold where hallucinations are characterized as Evidence Drops; proposes training-free, model-agnostic detector identifying hallucinations via worst-case evidence drop.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements over sequence-level baselines in selective accuracy and risk-coverage tradeoffs on GSM8K, MATH, and ProcessBench.

problem: Risk-averse offline RL must balance safety (avoiding catastrophic lower-tail risk) with achieving high returns, but prior methods sacrifice policy expressiveness or reliability.
approach: RAMAC couples an expressive generative actor (diffusion/flow) with a distributional critic optimizing Conditional Value-at-Risk combined with behavioral cloning; provides objective-level analysis showing BC suppresses OOD actions.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains in CVaR_{0.1} while maintaining strong returns on Stochastic-D4RL and illustrative 2D bandit.

problem: Standard SAT benchmarks conflate surface difficulty with structural phenomena determining satisfiability, limiting diagnostic evaluation of LLM reasoners.
approach: Introduces diagnostic benchmark for 2-SAT with parameterized families of structured 2-CNF formulas where satisfiability is tuned along interpretable axes, isolating distinct competencies and failure modes.
contribution: Reveals sharp performance transitions and brittleness regimes in LLM reasoners under targeted structural interventions even when surface statistics are held fixed.

problem: Equivariant generative models suffer from latent misalignment, where the intended group action does not match required transformations in latent space.
approach: Residual Latent Flow is a flow-based framework that corrects misaligned latents by learning residual corrections to improve compliance with underlying equivariance relations.
contribution: Significantly reduces latent misalignment and improves novel view synthesis quality under rotation groups SO(n).

problem: Neural operators struggle with general, highly variable boundary conditions, particularly when solutions are sensitive to boundary forcings.
approach: Maps boundary data to latent pseudo-extensions over the entire domain, allowing any operator architecture to consume boundary information; couples with domain-to-domain neural operators.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on 18 challenging PDE datasets with mixed-type boundary conditions, outperforming baselines without hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Current multi-model alignment strategies are pairwise, scaling quadratically and failing to yield a consistent global reference across three or more models.
approach: Adapts Generalized Procrustes Analysis to construct a shared orthogonal universe; proposes Geometry-Corrected Procrustes Alignment combining GPA-based universe with post-hoc directional correction.
contribution: Consistently improves any-to-any retrieval while retaining a practical shared reference space for model stitching.

problem: Protein-protein interaction prediction overlooks hierarchical protein organization and fails to integrate sequence, structure, and function modalities.
approach: MMM-PPI constructs embeddings bottom-up across three scales: micro-scale residue features, meso-scale multimodal motif encoder, macro-scale protein encoder jointly modeling motif importance and inter-modal correlations.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art multi-label PPI models, particularly under challenging data partitions and limited data scenarios.

problem: LLM agents with external and internal memory are exposed to severe extraction attacks but lack corresponding defenses.
approach: MemPot injects optimized honeypots into memory through two-stage optimization generating trap documents that maximize retrieval probability while remaining inconspicuous; models detection as Wald's Sequential Probability Ratio Test.
contribution: Achieves 50% improvement in detection AUROC and 80% increase in True Positive Rate under low False Positive Rate constraints with zero online inference latency.

problem: ANN-to-SNN conversion performs poorly in continuous control due to small action errors becoming temporally correlated and amplifying across decision steps.
approach: Cross-Step Residual Potential Initialization carries residual membrane potentials across decision steps to suppress temporally correlated errors in a gradient-free mechanism.
contribution: Substantially recovers lost performance during ANN-to-SNN conversion and highlights continuous control as critical benchmark for demonstrating how small errors amplify.

problem: One-step diffusion models for video super-resolution suffer from high computational cost and substantial model size, with naive quantization failing due to high dynamic range of latents.
approach: LSGQuant estimates layer sensitivity via calibration statistics and implements Variance-Oriented Layer Training Strategy; introduces Dynamic Range Adaptive Quantizer and Quantization-Aware Optimization.
contribution: Achieves nearly full-precision performance with significant speedup and significantly exceeds existing quantization techniques.

problem: Machine learning policies for branch-and-cut trained on local expert signals like strong branching can produce exponentially larger search trees than optimal.
approach: Identifies two sources of gap: misalignment between expert signals and overall tree size, and amplification of small discrepancies by branch-and-bound recursion.
contribution: Shows arbitrarily small perturbations and score discrepancies can produce exponentially different tree sizes, motivating data-driven methods better aligned with global objectives.

problem: Causal inference with unpaired data (observing covariates and outcomes under different conditions but not jointly) is challenging under hidden confounding.
approach: Casts the problem as instrumental variable regression with environment as instrument; proposes GMM-type estimator based on cross-fold sample splitting that works when observations per environment are few but environments are many.
contribution: Proves consistency as number of environments grows with constant sample size per environment; extends to sparse causal effects via L1-regularization.

problem: Vision Transformers remain vulnerable to adversarial examples with unclear theoretical foundations for adversarial training under ViT architectures.
approach: Provides first theoretical analysis showing adversarial training enables ViTs to achieve nearly zero robust training loss and robust generalization error under benign overfitting conditions.
contribution: Demonstrates strong generalization in presence of overfitting under moderate perturbation budget and signal-to-noise conditions.

problem: Diffusion language models generate text slowly by decoding only a few tokens per step; parallel decoding degrades quality by violating conditional independence.
approach: SPEED uses sharpened teacher distillation at training time with temperature-scaled KL and masked LM loss; at inference, Slow-Fast Decoding partitions tokens by sensitivity using Jensen-Shannon Divergence.
contribution: Achieves up to 12.2x speedup on LLaDA-8B and 6.7x on Dream-7B while maintaining accuracy close to greedy decoding.

problem: Foundation models for chaotic system forecasting fail to capture multi-scale temporal structures and heterogeneous spectral characteristics across diverse systems.
approach: ChaosNexus uses ScaleFormer architecture with hierarchical patch sizes and Mixture-of-Experts layers; conditions forecasts on learned frequency fingerprint providing global spectral view.
contribution: Achieves superior fidelity in long-term attractor statistics while maintaining competitive point-wise accuracy; zero-shot weather forecasting achieves mean error below 1°C for 5-day predictions.

problem: Autoregressive video diffusion suffers from visual error accumulation including fidelity and motion degradation during extended rollouts.
approach: Deep Forcing uses Deep Sink to preserve sink tokens with realigned temporal RoPE and Participative Compression for importance-aware KV cache pruning, both training-free.
contribution: Enables over 12x length extrapolation without sacrificing speed while improving visual fidelity and motion compared to prior methods.

problem: Medical imaging datasets with extensive tabular attributes often have only partial attributes available at inference, requiring methods robust to missing data.
approach: RoVTL uses contrastive pretraining with missingness as augmentation and downstream tuning with Tabular More vs. Fewer loss ranking performance by data completeness.
contribution: Achieves superior robustness to missing tabular data on cardiac MRI from UK Biobank and generalizes to external datasets and natural images.

problem: Diffusion language models suffer from high inference latency because traditional techniques like key-value caching are incompatible with their bidirectional attention.
approach: dLLM-Cache combines long-interval prompt caching with partial response updates guided by feature similarity, exploiting that most tokens remain stable across denoising steps.
contribution: Achieves up to 9.1x FLOPs reduction on LongBench while maintaining competitive output quality, bringing dLLM inference latency near ARM levels.

problem: Convergence rate analysis for AdamW-style Shampoo remains unclear, particularly when unifying one-sided and two-sided preconditioning.
approach: Establishes convergence rate using nuclear norm gradient measurement, showing O(sqrt(m+n)C/K^{1/4}) for matrix parameters of size (m,n).
contribution: Proves convergence rate analogous to optimal SGD under ideal spectral conditions with balanced dimensions.

problem: Popular deep learning optimizers like Lion and Muon lack theoretical grounding, and existing Stochastic Frank-Wolfe methods do not handle heavy-tailed noise.
approach: Interprets Lion and Muon as Stochastic Frank-Wolfe variants and develops robust versions handling heavy-tailed noise with convergence guarantees on compact convex sets.
contribution: Provides convergence guarantees in Frank-Wolfe gap and derives new Lion/Muon variants better accommodating gradient noise.

problem: Terminal embeddings for coresets cannot be linear and thus cannot directly preserve linear structures in time-series clustering.
approach: Generalizes terminal embeddings to affine line-segments using Johnson-Lindenstrauss embeddings, enabling dimension-free coresets for clustering time-series under Fréchet distance.
contribution: Provides first dimension-free coresets for time-series clustering with empirical results showing favorable comparison to PCA.

problem: Existing convergence guarantees for discretized underdamped Langevin dynamics scale polynomially with ambient dimension, yielding vacuous bounds for high-dimensional problems.
approach: Refines KL local error framework to dimension-free setting, proving bounds depend on tr(H) rather than d, where H upper bounds the Hessian.
contribution: Closes the gap with first dimension-free KL divergence bounds for discretized underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo.

problem: Classical kernel density estimators generalize but suffer from curse of dimensionality; neural score models are precise but require retraining for each distribution.
approach: DiScoFormer is an equivariant Transformer mapping i.i.d. samples to both density and score; proves self-attention recovers normalized KDE, generalizing kernel methods.
contribution: Converges faster with higher precision than KDE; provides high-fidelity plug-in score oracle for score-debiased KDE and PDEs.

problem: Unconstrained neural critics for divergence estimation are prone to instability, limiting reliable variational inference.
approach: Constrains critic to RKHS ball with Random Fourier Features approximation yielding linear-time objective; provides unified four-term error decomposition analysis.
contribution: Outperforms baselines in stability; applying spectral regularization to GANs significantly enhances capture of high-frequency data components.

problem: Purely numerical RL feedback causes performance plateaus, ineffective self-reflection, and persistent reasoning failures in LLMs.
approach: Critique-GRPO integrates both natural language critiques and numerical rewards, enabling simultaneous learning from initial responses and critique-guided refinements.
contribution: Achieves 15.0-21.6% average Pass@1 improvements on Qwen models and 7.3% on Llama-3.2 across eight reasoning tasks; +16.7% on AIME via self-critiquing.
